sourceType: Official Government of Punjab tourism website
note: Facts extracted below; prose summaries are written in our own words, not copied verbatim from the source.
about: Doaba-region district known as the 'Paris of Punjab' for its Indo-French architecture, shaped by Maharaja Jagatjit Singh's admiration for European styles. Also home to Sultanpur Lodhi, where Guru Nanak Dev Ji attained enlightenment in 1499.

places.name: Jagatjit Palace
places.facts: Built 1908 by Maharaja Jagatjit Singh, modelled on the Palace of Versailles; Indo-Saracenic architecture; now houses Sainik School.

places.name: Moorish Mosque
places.facts: Completed 1930, designed by French architect M. Manteaux, inspired by the Grand Mosque of Marrakesh.

places.name: Panch Mandir
places.facts: 'Five Temples'; built during the reign of Sardar Fateh Singh Ahluwalia; silver entrance door.

places.name: Kanjli Wetland
places.facts: Ramsar wetland of international importance, created 1870 via headworks on the Kali Bein; ~490 hectares.

places.name: Sultanpur Lodhi
places.facts: Where Guru Nanak Dev Ji attained enlightenment on the banks of the Kali Bein in 1499; home to Gurdwara Ber Sahib.

places.name: Pushpa Gujral Science City
places.facts: One of the largest science centres in northern India; interactive exhibits, planetarium.

places.name: Shalimar Garden
places.facts: Landscaped public garden from the princely era.

howToReach.air: Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar (~75km)
howToReach.road: ~20km from Jalandhar, ~75km from Amritsar, ~165km from Chandigarh
